subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but only maintainers can choose whether operators may hide warnings that currently protect users from silent false success and how a new policy should coexist with the shipped boolean.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add an `all` default with explicit final/off semantics after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow remaining work to docs or specific channel leaks.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle channel-specific or tool-class-specific leaks before designing a shared policy.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add an `all` default with explicit final/off semantics after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged warning-policy fix that explicitly scoped this issue as the remaining broader config decision.
